pages.abstract: The Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA) was a United States federal law passed by the 104th United States Congress and signed into law by President Bill Clinton on September 21, 1996. nytimes_articles.headline: Living Dangerously
nytimes_articles.abstract:
We lived in Providence during the year everyone was worried about electrical waves. As I recall, it didn't matter if the waves came from something big like power lines or small like coffee makers. Waves of any kind were suspect. Even now, I have no reason to play down this threat. I don't know what it is, really. But there was a big gray transformer on a utility pole in front of our house that would buzz and click. It was a fine house in many ways, with a fireplace and skeleton keys. My wife and I had just had a child. ''The sooner we get away from this transformer, the better off we'll be,'' I remember thinking.

 After Providence, we lived down by the ocean for a couple of years and then moved to northwestern Connecticut. The house we live in now, like the one in Providence, drew our attention with its honest old-time appearance. The windows are tall and wood framed, and when summer ends, I unhook the screens, put them away and hang the storms, just as homeowners have been doing and hating for many decades before me. Through the window right now, I see treeline and grass and a rail fence and a swing set for the child, who is 5 going on 6. No transformers border the property, but the tap water is laced with radon.
